books.title: Bhagavad Gītā
books.credit: Ancient Sanskrit text in IAST. English renderings prepared for this sample.

2.roman:
karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana
mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stv akarmaṇi
2.english: Your claim is to action alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit of action be your motive, and do not become attached to inaction.

2.roman:
yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate
2.english: Act with steadiness in yoga, Dhanañjaya, letting go of attachment. Remain even-minded in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.

2.roman:
dūreṇa hy avaraṃ karma buddhi-yogād dhanañjaya
buddhau śaraṇam anviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phala-hetavaḥ
2.english: Action done for its fruits falls far short of the yoga of discernment, Dhanañjaya. Seek refuge in discernment. Those who act for the fruits are pitiable.

2.roman:
buddhi-yukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte
tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam
2.english: One grounded in discernment sets aside both good and bad deeds here. So devote yourself to yoga. Yoga is skill in action.

3.roman:
tasmād asaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara
asakto hy ācaran karma param āpnoti pūruṣaḥ
3.english: So always perform the work that should be done, without attachment. A person who acts without attachment attains the highest.

3.roman:
karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhim āsthitā janakādayaḥ
loka-saṃgraham evāpi sampaśyan kartum arhasi
3.english: Janaka and others attained perfection through action itself. You should also act with the welfare of the world in view.

3.roman:
yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ
sa yat pramāṇaṃ kurute lokas tad anuvartate
3.english: Whatever an exemplary person does, others do likewise. The world follows the standard that person sets.
